limitations: The abstract reports a fetal-placental unit value, not a fetus-only CO2 production rate; placental metabolism is included in the stated unit.
Although the unit is printed as mL/min per kg, the abstract does not identify the mass denominator, so it cannot be converted to an absolute fetal or fetal-placental mL/min value.
The abstract reports 12 normal women undergoing elective cesarean but does not specify gestational age or endpoint-specific n for the CO2 estimate.
The value is estimated indirectly by maternal calorimetry using the Bohr principle, not measured as fetal umbilical arteriovenous CO2 flux.
Only the PubMed abstract was available in this intake; no individual measurements, variance definition beyond SEM, or source full text is available.
This is a candidate historical context value, not a gestation-specific requirement, safety margin, or artificial-placenta design specification.

limitations: The only recovered human volumetric CO2-production result in this screen is an abstract-level fetal-placental-unit estimate from an elective-cesarean cohort; the abstract does not report gestational age, endpoint-specific n, or mass denominator.
The 2006 Wiberg cohort covers term deliveries at 37-43 weeks and reports a fractional CO2 index per birthweight, not an absolute mL/min flux; it is not a 24-28 week production benchmark.
A-Maze-Ox CO2 targets are calculated from gas-composition assumptions and mean UV flows; they are not directly observed fetal CO2 production requirements.
Preemie-Ox vCO2 and A-Maze-Ox CT are in-vitro device results under different blood, flow and inlet-gas conditions; numerical ratios are descriptive only and do not establish adequacy.
